meta.description: Gross domestic product divided by midyear population. GDP at purchaser prices includes all resident producers plus taxes minus subsidies.
meta.source: World Bank, World Development Indicators
meta.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater economic output per person. Compare within regions for meaningful benchmarks -- cost of living varies widely.

meta.description: Average number of years a newborn is expected to live under current mortality patterns.
meta.source: World Bank, derived from UN Population Division
meta.interpretation: Reflects overall health system quality and living conditions. Global average is around 73 years. Above 80 is typical for high-income countries.

meta.description: Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel burning, cement manufacturing, and gas flaring, divided by population.
meta.source: Global Carbon Project / World Bank
meta.interpretation: Measured in metric tons. Global average is ~4.5t. Oil-producing states and industrialized nations typically exceed 10t per capita.

meta.description: Annual percentage change in consumer prices. Reflects the rate at which purchasing power is eroded.
meta.source: International Monetary Fund via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Central banks typically target 2%. Above 10% is considered high inflation. Hyperinflation exceeds 50% monthly.

meta.description: Share of the labor force that is without work but available and seeking employment (ILO modeled estimate).
meta.source: International Labour Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Below 5% is considered full employment. 5-10% is moderate. Above 15% signals serious economic distress.

meta.description: Central government debt as percentage of GDP. Includes domestic and foreign liabilities.
meta.source: World Bank, International Monetary Fund
meta.interpretation: Below 60% is generally considered sustainable (EU Maastricht criterion). Japan exceeds 250%, the US is above 120%.

meta.description: Total fertility rate: average number of children a woman would bear over her lifetime under current age-specific rates.
meta.source: UN Population Division via World Bank
meta.interpretation: 2.1 is replacement level. Below 1.5 indicates demographic decline. Above 4 is common in Sub-Saharan Africa.

meta.description: Individuals who have used the Internet in the last 3 months via any device including mobile phones.
meta.source: International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
meta.interpretation: Percentage of population. Above 90% indicates high digital connectivity. Below 30% suggests significant digital divide.

meta.description: Military expenditure as share of gross domestic product. Includes armed forces, defense ministries, and paramilitary forces.
meta.source: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) via World Bank
meta.interpretation: NATO target is 2% of GDP. Global average is ~2.2%. Above 4% indicates high militarization. Some conflict states exceed 6%.

meta.description: Total population based on the de facto definition, counting all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.
meta.source: UN Population Division via World Bank
meta.interpretation: India and China each exceed 1.4 billion. The median country has around 10 million inhabitants.

meta.description: Midyear population divided by land area in square kilometers.
meta.source: World Bank, World Development Indicators
meta.interpretation: Global average is ~60 per km2. City states like Singapore exceed 8,000. Mongolia has about 2.

meta.description: Share of the population living in urban areas as defined by national statistical offices.
meta.source: UN Population Division via World Bank
meta.interpretation: The world crossed 50% urban around 2007. Above 80% is typical for highly developed economies.

meta.description: Share of the population that is 65 years or older.
meta.source: UN Population Division via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Above 20% indicates an aged society (Japan, Italy). Sub-Saharan Africa is mostly below 4%.

meta.description: Annual percentage growth rate of GDP at market prices based on constant local currency.
meta.source: World Bank, World Development Indicators
meta.interpretation: Mature economies grow 1-3% per year. Above 6% is rapid growth. Negative values indicate recession.

meta.description: Number of international inbound tourists arriving per year.
meta.source: World Tourism Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: France leads with ~90 million arrivals per year. COVID cut global tourism by ~70% in 2020.

meta.description: Passengers carried by air carriers registered in the country, domestic and international.
meta.source: International Civil Aviation Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Reflects both market size and hub status. The US and China each carry over 500 million passengers per year.

meta.description: Number of medical doctors, including generalists and specialists, per 1,000 people.
meta.source: World Health Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: The WHO considers fewer than 1 per 1,000 a critical shortage. Europe averages 3-5.

meta.description: Current health expenditure including public and private spending as share of GDP.
meta.source: World Health Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: The US spends over 16% of GDP. Most of Europe spends 9-12%. Below 4% is common in low-income countries.

meta.description: Probability per 1,000 live births that a newborn dies before reaching age five.
meta.source: UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation
meta.interpretation: Below 5 in most high-income countries. Global progress cut the rate by more than half since 2000.

meta.description: Total alcohol consumed per adult (15+) per year, in liters of pure alcohol.
meta.source: World Health Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Central and Eastern Europe lead with over 12 liters. Muslim-majority countries are typically below 1.

meta.description: Share of adults with a body mass index of 25 or higher.
meta.source: World Health Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Pacific island states exceed 80%. Global average is around 40% and rising.

meta.description: Estimated deaths from road traffic injuries per 100,000 population.
meta.source: World Health Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Europe averages below 10. Parts of Africa and Southeast Asia exceed 25 despite far fewer vehicles.

meta.description: Land under natural or planted forest of at least 5 meters, as share of total land area.
meta.source: Food and Agriculture Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Suriname and Guyana exceed 90%. Desert nations are near 0%. The global average is ~31%.

meta.description: Share of the population with access to electricity.
meta.source: World Bank, Sustainable Energy for All
meta.interpretation: Universal in high and middle income countries. Sub-Saharan Africa averages around 50%.

meta.description: Mobile cellular subscriptions per 100 people, including multiple SIMs per person.
meta.source: International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
meta.interpretation: Values above 100 are common since many people hold several SIM cards.

meta.description: Share of women aged 15 and older who are economically active (ILO modeled estimate).
meta.source: International Labour Organization via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Nordic countries exceed 60%. Some countries in the Middle East and South Asia are below 25%.

meta.description: General government expenditure on education as share of GDP.
meta.source: UNESCO Institute for Statistics via World Bank
meta.interpretation: UNESCO recommends 4-6% of GDP. Nordic countries typically spend 6-8%.

meta.description: Gross domestic expenditure on research and development as share of GDP.
meta.source: UNESCO Institute for Statistics via World Bank
meta.interpretation: Israel and South Korea lead with ~5%. The EU target is 3%. Most countries spend below 1%.

meta.description: Active duty military personnel plus paramilitary forces if trained and equipped like the military.
meta.source: International Institute for Strategic Studies via World Bank
meta.interpretation: China maintains the largest force at over 2 million. Iceland has no standing army.

meta.description: Measures the quality of liberal democracy including individual liberties, rule of law, judicial independence, and checks on executive power.
meta.source: V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg
meta.interpretation: Scale 0 to 1. Values above 0.7 indicate consolidated liberal democracies. Below 0.3 suggests autocratic governance.

meta.description: Measures political corruption including executive, legislative, and judicial corruption as well as public sector bribery.
meta.source: V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg
meta.interpretation: Scale 0 to 1. Lower values indicate less corruption. Values above 0.7 suggest systemic corruption across institutions.

_source: World Bank API + V-Dem v14 curated data
